aspectTitle: Error text is fluent and field-identifying but factually wrong for the value entered / constraint violated (boilerplate mismatch)
aspectDescription: A page shows a non-empty, grammatically descriptive, field-identifying error message that satisfies rule 36b590's 'describes the cause or how to resolve it' check at the string level, but the described cause is factually wrong for the value the user actually entered or the constraint that was actually violated. The text reads as a competent error description in isolation, so it passes every programmatic facet of the rule, but it misidentifies the nature of the error and so defeats the SC's core intent that the user 'can determine what is wrong'. Examples: a phone field that says 'Remove letter
scenario: Telecom line-activation wizard, post-submit error state. Phone field is digits-only; the retained value is the all-digit string '12025550143'. The visible, aria-describedby-associated error reads 'Mobile number is invalid. Remove letters and parentheses from your phone number, then try again.' — describing a cause (letters/parentheses) that is factually absent from the value. The real defect (an 11-digit string for a 10-digit field) is never described.
mechanism: Boilerplate mismatch: a fluent, field-identifying error asserts a cause that did not occur for THIS value. The value (all digits) does not exhibit the named defect (letters/parentheses), so the error misidentifies the nature of the error and the user cannot determine what is actually wrong.

aspectTitle: Post-submit page suppresses the error: form silently re-displayed (or shows a neutral/success banner) after a real validation failure — trigger-and-observe failure of NO indicator
aspectDescription: The SC's most-emphasized procedural limb is trigger-and-observe: submit invalid input, then check whether an error is conveyed in text. The failure the Understanding calls out FIRST is re-displaying the form 'without providing any hint that the submission failed'. On a self-contained page this is staged as the post-submit STATE: the page representing 'the user submitted invalid input and the server bounced it' shows the form again with the bad value retained but NO error message — or worse, shows a neutral/green confirmation that does not mention the failure. A tool inspecting this page finds
scenario: Riverbend Library membership registration re-displayed under the heading 'Submission received' after the server bounced the submission: Age field still shows '0' (below the stated minimum of 1), required Email is still empty, and there is no error text anywhere. Variant A (bare silent re-display). HEAD-prevalence; content-domain government/civic, server-rendered POST result page, native form.
mechanism: An input error was automatically detected (server enforced min=1 and required Email) but is described in zero text; the 'Submission received' heading actively makes a screen-reader user believe the submission succeeded (G83 warning), while the retained out-of-range Age '0' and empty required Email are the only evidence of the failure, neither flagged as an error.

scenario: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): the same Riverbend Library membership flow as case-01, but the genuine SUCCESS result after VALID input (Age 34, a real email). The server accepted the data and rendered a true confirmation — a read-only summary of the accepted values, a real membership number (RVB-2026-08831), and next steps — with no editable form re-displayed and legitimately no error message. aspectTitle: Inline error message is visually placed next to the WRONG field, with no programmatic association to check
aspectDescription: A self-contained page renders a descriptive error message physically below / next to a field, but the message's text refers to a DIFFERENT field than the one it visually sits under, and there is no aria-describedby tying it to any control (so no programmatic association exists to evaluate). A sighted user reads the message against the field it appears to annotate and is misled about which item is in error. Because identification by visual proximity ('errors inline ... next to the specific fields') is an explicitly sufficient method under the SC, the message passes every programmatic facet of 3
scenario: E-commerce checkout payment row (Card number / Expiry / CVV) in a flex row. The CVV value '12' is the truly-invalid input, but the error 'CVV must be exactly 3 digits.' is rendered in the message slot under the Card number field, and the Card number input carries the red invalid border. No aria-describedby anywhere.
mechanism: Identification rests solely on presentation (proximity) because no aria-describedby/for-id linkage exists. The error span sits in the Card-number field block while its text names CVV, so by visual proximity the message identifies the wrong field; the field actually in error (CVV) appears unflagged. SC 3.3.1 'the item that is in error is identified' fails because presentation points at Card number, not CVV.

Each individual statement may be a fluent error description (passing 36b590 at the mes
scenario: GOV.UK council-tax reduction form: top-of-form red error summary announces 'We found 2 errors' and lists Full name + Email, but both render filled and unflagged; the only field actually in error (Telephone, value 'ring me weekdays') has a red border, inline message and aria-invalid=true and is never named. Wrong count AND wrong fields named.
